overview: This report covers 38 unseen announcements: 11 HIGH PRIORITY, 12 RELATED / POSSIBLY INTERESTING, and 15 LOW PRIORITY. Central themes include entropy-controlled Lyapunov continuity, exact fractal projection dimensions, periodic maximizing measures on shifts, symbolic coding of the basilica, and structural invariants of group actions and flows. Related work concerns geodesic foliations, dynamical limit laws, complex pullback spectra, invariant manifolds, circle cohomology and singular invariant distributions. paper.title: Besicovitch Pseudo Almost Periodic Stochastic Processes and Their Applications to Delayed Stochastic Neural Networks
paper.abstract: The Besicovitch almost periodic concept is a generalization of the Bohr, Stepanov, and Weyl almost periodic concepts and, in a certain sense, has broader coverage and weaker conditions. However, the concept of pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes in the Besicovitch sense has not yet been systematically proposed, which limits the characterization of the complex oscillatory behavior of a broader class of stochastic non-autonomous systems. This paper proposes the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes. As an application of this concept, we study the existence of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic solutions in distribution for a class of stochastic delayed neural networks in which all parameters except the time delays are pseudo almost periodic and establish stability criteria for such solutions in the $p$-th mean sense. The work of this paper fills the gap caused by the lack of the concept of Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes and provides a new conceptual tool and analytical approach for characterizing the complex oscillatory behavior of stochastic differential equations and stochastic neural network systems.

analysis.relevance_note: Generalized almost periodicity and distributional recurrence give an indirect connection to recurrent dynamics, although the application concerns stochastic neural networks.
analysis.tldr: A Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic-process concept supports existence and mean-stability results for delayed stochastic neural networks.
analysis.problem: Formulate Besicovitch pseudo almost periodicity for stochastic processes and apply it to distributional solutions.
analysis.main_result: The authors introduce Besicovitch pseudo almost periodic stochastic processes and establish existence of solutions that are pseudo almost periodic in distribution for a class of stochastic delayed neural networks whose parameters, apart from time delays, are pseudo almost periodic. They also give stability criteria in the \(p\)-th mean sense. The precise process definition, admissibility assumptions and stability inequalities: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Generalized almost periodic stochastic processes and recurrent distributional solutions.

paper.title: Cyclicity of period annuli of quadratic codimension four centers
paper.abstract: Quadratic systems with a center fall into four classes: Hamiltonian $Q_3^H$, reversible $Q_3^R$, generalized Lotka--Volterra $Q_3^{LV}$, and codimension-four $Q_4$. Before this work, the cyclicity of period annuli under quadratic perturbations had been completely determined for $Q_3^H$, whereas only certain special cases had been resolved for $Q_3^R$, $Q_3^{LV}$ and $Q_4$. In this paper, we establish that the period annulus of every center in $Q_4$ has cyclicity three under quadratic perturbations, thereby proving \.{Z}o{\l}{\k{a}}dek's 1994 conjecture for this class. The proof combines Picard--Fuchs equations with a Chebyshev criterion. Its key step is a strict Wronskian inequality for two ratios of elliptic integrals on their entire interval of definition. We establish this inequality by constructing a comparison function and excluding a first zero of the Wronskian. The Chebyshev property avoids the two additional zeros allowed by the second-order differential reduction used in earlier proofs.

analysis.relevance_note: Quadratic period-annulus cyclicity is an ODE bifurcation problem without a central entropy, symbolic, dimensional or group-action component here.

paper.title: Quantifying combined rate- and noise-induced transitions in a multiscale system
paper.abstract: Excitations in multiscale dynamical systems produce persistent but impermanent excursions away from a quiescent state. A novel mechanism for inducing excitations, through a combination of rate-dependent parametric and stochastic forcing, is discussed using the FitzHugh-Nagumo model as an example. In the absence of noise, a quasithreshold separating the state space between supercritical and subcritical behaviour is defined with respect to slow manifolds associated with the metastable excited state. This is formulated in an autonomous system framework, which can be obtained via a compactification of time. Techniques from singular perturbation theory elucidate how canard trajectories shape the geometric structure of the quasithreshold as the system's pullback attractor moves through it. The probability with which weakly stochastically driven sample paths travel through the quasithreshold and undertake (i) solely noise-induced and (ii) combined rate- and noise-induced excitations is estimated numerically for each of the corresponding forcing scenarios, using the adaptive multilevel splitting algorithm. The probability of weak stochastic forcing preventing a rate-induced excitation, which occurs deterministically, is likewise estimated. This quantifies the different rates at which the probability of each transition scenario scales exponentially with the noise strength, in accordance with sample path large deviation principles. It is revealed that a combination of (deterministically subcritical) parametric and stochastic forcing is exponentially more likely to induce excitations than stochastic forcing alone, which is attributed to the pullback attractor and quasithreshold converging towards one another.

analysis.relevance_note: Excitation probabilities in a stochastic FitzHugh–Nagumo model are primarily multiscale physical modeling and numerical rare-event analysis.

paper.title: On the non existence of minimal non-uniquely ergodic 4-IETs with flips
paper.abstract: The existence of minimal non uniquely ergodic oriented IETs of n intervals requires that n>= 4 by Th. 2.12 from (W. A. Veech, Interval exchange transformations, J. Anal. Math., 1978); moreover, for n=4 there exist examples of minimal non uniquely ergodic 4-IETs with two independent invariant measures, see (M. Keane, Non-ergodic interval exchange transformations, Israel J. Math., 1977). For the non oriented case, also called IETs with flips, the first examples of minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs were built in (A. Linero Bas and G. Soler L\'{o}pez, Minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs with flips, J. Differential Equations, 2023). However, the examples are (10,k)-IETs (k is the number of flips, 1<= k<= 10). Since there are no minimal (n,k)-IETs for n<= 3, it is interesting to decide if, as in the orientable case, there exist minimal non uniquely ergodic IETs with flips and four intervals. Our Main Theorem answers this question in the negative.

analysis.relevance_note: Minimality and unique ergodicity of interval exchanges directly concern topological and invariant-measure dynamics.
analysis.tldr: There are no minimal non-uniquely ergodic interval exchanges with flips on four intervals.
analysis.problem: Determine whether four-interval exchanges with flips can be minimal without being uniquely ergodic.
analysis.main_result: The main theorem rules out minimal non-uniquely ergodic four-interval exchanges with flips. The abstract contrasts this with oriented four-interval examples having two independent invariant measures and with previously constructed ten-interval examples with flips. It also recalls that there are no minimal interval exchanges with flips on at most three intervals. No existence assertion for minimal four-interval exchanges with flips follows from the stated nonexistence theorem. The proof methods and additional structural criteria: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Minimal interval exchanges, flips and unique ergodicity.

paper.title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
paper.abstract: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.

analysis.relevance_note: A geodesic-foliation characterization of closed-orbit topology gives a clear structural connection to geodesic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: A Riemannian two-torus has no contractible closed geodesics exactly when it admits a geodesic foliation.
analysis.problem: Characterize Riemannian two-tori without contractible closed geodesics.
analysis.main_result: For a two-dimensional Riemannian torus, absence of contractible closed geodesics is equivalent to existence of a geodesic foliation. The proof techniques, foliation regularity and further quantitative consequences: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Geodesic dynamics, torus topology and foliations.

paper.title: Linear images of graphs of vector-valued affine fractal interpolation functions
paper.abstract: We determine the Hausdorff and box dimensions of every linear image of the graph of a vector-valued affine fractal interpolation function with positive vertical factors. The same formula holds for signed factors under a rank condition on the active branches. Outside an explicit finite union of hyperplanes in the space of vertical factors it holds simultaneously for all choices of interpolation knots and all linear images. The dimension is determined by the branch contractions, the rank of the projected deviations from the endpoint line, and the affine dimension of the projected knots. The proof gives uniform entropy estimates over bounded slopes for tilted projections of homogeneous triangular systems. Permutations of words with prescribed symbol frequencies then transfer the dimension estimates to unequal branch contractions. For the homogeneous systems covered by the entropy estimate, we also compute the exact dimensions of Bernoulli measures and their tilted projections. Examples with exceptional factors exhibit distinct Hausdorff and box dimensions.

analysis.relevance_note: Exact Hausdorff and box dimensions, entropy estimates and dimensions of projected Bernoulli measures directly match the strongest interests.
analysis.tldr: Dimensions of all linear images of affine fractal-interpolation graphs are determined for positive vertical factors, with qualified extensions to signed factors.
analysis.problem: Compute dimensions of linear images of vector-valued affine fractal-interpolation graphs and associated measures.
analysis.main_result: The authors determine Hausdorff and box dimensions of every linear image of the graph of a vector-valued affine fractal interpolation function with positive vertical factors. The same formula applies to signed factors under a rank condition on active branches. Outside an explicit finite union of hyperplanes in vertical-factor space, it holds simultaneously for all interpolation knots and all linear images. The dimension depends on branch contractions, the rank of projected deviations from the endpoint line, and the affine dimension of projected knots. Uniform entropy estimates over bounded slopes for tilted projections of homogeneous triangular systems, followed by permutations of words with prescribed symbol frequencies, handle unequal branch contractions. For homogeneous systems covered by that estimate, exact dimensions of Bernoulli measures and tilted projections are also computed. Exceptional-factor examples have distinct Hausdorff and box dimensions. The dimension formulas, rank condition and exceptional hyperplanes: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Uniform entropy estimates for tilted projections
Permutations of words with prescribed symbol frequencies
analysis.context: Fractal interpolation, linear projections, entropy estimates and measure dimensions.

paper.title: Singular rational S-functions of second-order ODEs: structure, degree bounds and a Kovacic-type search
authors: L. A. C. P. da Mota
paper.abstract: For a rational second-order ODE $y''=phi(x,y,y')$, the $S$-function method reduces the search for a first integral to finding a rational solution $S$ of the Riccati-type equation $X(S)=S^2+phi_z S-phi_y$ along the total-derivative field $X$. The standard ansatz $S=P/N^k$, with $N=den(phi)$, misses every $S$ with poles outside $N=0$. Such singular solutions cannot be avoided: for point transforms of linear equations without hyperexponential solutions we describe every quasi-regular $S$ explicitly, and for a generic transformation none exists. We then determine the structure of singular solutions. Outside $N$ every pole is simple, with residue $-1$, and is not a Darboux surface; along non-characteristic factors of $N$ the leading polar coefficient is free Cauchy data; and the only unknown denominator is a squarefree polynomial $D$, which enters a linear equation. A Newton-polygon analysis at infinity gives the polynomial part up to a correction of bounded weight. The weighted degree of $D$ is determined exactly when the excess is zero and the top Riccati equation has no algebraic solution, and is bounded by residues of the top field otherwise, conditionally on the vanishing of that correction. The dependence of $D$ on $x$ is obtained, without a degree bound, from the rational solutions of a linear differential system. These results give a certified search procedure, implemented twice, which finds the singular $S$ of nine non-Liouvillian pull-backs of the Airy and Bessel equations. In one regime it is a decision procedure; for instance, it proves that $y''=xy+1$ has no rational $S$.

analysis.relevance_note: Certified searches for rational first-integral auxiliary functions are mainly symbolic ODE integrability algorithms, rather than symbolic dynamics.

paper.title: From the Deterministic Hook Effect to Stochastic Reliability in Ternary Complex Formation
paper.abstract: Ternary binding systems occur in signaling, scaffold-mediated assembly, and targeted protein degradation. A mediator brings two partners into a productive ternary complex, but excess mediator can hold them in separate binary complexes. Consequently, ternary complex formation can increase and then decrease as the mediator dose increases, producing the hook effect. Deterministic dose-response curves describe the average behavior but do not indicate whether individual small compartments reliably form the complex. A minimal reversible binding network was studied using deterministic equations, exact stochastic simulations, and a simple catalytic extension. The deterministic model recovered the hook-shaped response. In stochastic simulations, small volumes often failed to accumulate the required number of complexes, even where the deterministic prediction was favorable. At low mediator doses, failure reflected a shortage of mediator molecules; at high doses, material accumulated in free or binary-bound forms. Larger volumes increased the range of mediator doses supporting reliable formation, while stricter copy-number thresholds narrowed that range. Faster ternary-complex completion or slower breakup improved reliability. In the catalytic model, product formation also depended on how early productive complexes formed. These results show why a favorable average binding response does not necessarily ensure reliable assembly in small reaction volumes.

analysis.relevance_note: Deterministic and stochastic ternary-binding reliability is biological reaction-network modeling without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: Sections and Constant Fields of Postcritically Finite Rational Maps
paper.abstract: We relate the constant fields of generic preimage towers to two invariants of geometric monodromy. Bounded section indices characterize branching of the closed action and imply a finite constant extension. Unbounded finite-level abelianization orders force an infinite cyclotomic subextension. For a quadratic rational map with hyperbolic orbifold, we compute the section indices and abelianizations at every sufficiently large level and obtain an infinite real cyclotomic subextension. We also give a branching criterion for quadratic maps with neither critical point periodic and formulate three conjectures about the discrete action, the constants, and the case of bounded abelianizations with unbounded section indices.

analysis.relevance_note: Section indices and abelianizations of geometric-monodromy actions make group-action invariants central to the arithmetic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Geometric-monodromy invariants control finite constant extensions and force infinite cyclotomic subextensions in generic preimage towers.
analysis.problem: Relate constant fields of generic preimage towers to section indices and finite-level abelianizations.
analysis.main_result: Bounded section indices characterize branching of the closed action and imply a finite constant extension. Unbounded finite-level abelianization orders force an infinite cyclotomic subextension. For a quadratic rational map with hyperbolic orbifold, section indices and abelianizations are computed at every sufficiently large level, yielding an infinite real cyclotomic subextension. A branching criterion is given for quadratic maps with neither critical point periodic. Three further statements concerning the discrete action, constants, and bounded abelianizations with unbounded section indices are formulated as conjectures. The invariant definitions, explicit computations, criterion and conjecture statements: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Computation of geometric-monodromy section indices and finite-level abelianizations
analysis.context: Postcritically finite rational maps, preimage towers and monodromy actions.

paper.title: Data-driven framework for invariant manifold identification in multiscale systems
paper.abstract: Multiscale dynamical systems often exhibit fast transient behavior followed by slow evolution on a low-dimensional attracting manifold, on which their long-term dynamics unfold. Identifying this structure directly from data remains challenging when the governing equations, Jacobians, and fast-slow variable partitions are unknown. In this work, we propose a fully data-driven framework for timescale decomposition, slow invariant manifold (SIM) approximation, and reduced-order model identification. A sparse-regression surrogate of the vector field is reconstructed from the data, and its Jacobian, estimated with a matrix-free Krylov method, is analysed with Computational Singular Perturbation diagnostics. The resulting fast-slow partition guides the learning of explicit SIM algebraic representations through regression, and the reduced model follows by restricting the dynamics to it. For a linear stochastic system, this regression agrees with the Mori-Zwanzig projection at leading order in the timescale ratio. We demonstrate the validity of the framework on an illustrative linear system, the Michaelis-Menten model, a biofilm growth model, and a five-dimensional target-mediated drug disposition (TMDD) model. The method accurately identifies fast variables, reconstructs slow invariant manifolds, and generates accurate reduced models. Furthermore, we map the performance boundaries of the framework under sparse sampling and measurement noise, showing robust recovery for low-dimensional systems and highlighting data-requirement limits in higher dimensions. These results demonstrate that interpretable multiscale reduction can be achieved directly from time-series data, without requiring explicit prior knowledge of the underlying fast/slow timescale separation.

analysis.relevance_note: Data-driven multiscale reduction and slow-manifold approximation are computational model-identification work without a central profile theme.

paper.title: From Limit Theorems to Mixing Limit Theorems
paper.abstract: Following the work of Gou\"ezel, we give an alternative proof, under weaker assumptions, of a result of Arana-Herrera and Forni, which provides a general method for upgrading limit theorems for cocycles over dynamical systems to mixing limit theorems.

analysis.relevance_note: Cocycles and mixing limit theorems give a substantial ergodic-theory connection, although no entropy or dimension statement is supplied.
analysis.tldr: An alternative proof under weaker assumptions upgrades limit theorems for dynamical cocycles to mixing limit theorems.
analysis.problem: Obtain mixing versions of limit theorems for cocycles over dynamical systems.
analysis.main_result: Following the cited work of Gouëzel, the author gives an alternative proof, under weaker assumptions, of the cited Arana-Herrera–Forni result providing a general upgrade from cocycle limit theorems to mixing limit theorems. The weaker assumptions, cocycle class, precise limit laws and technical proof mechanism: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Dynamical cocycles, limit theorems and mixing.

paper.title: Entropic continuity of Lyapunov exponents in arbitrary dimension
paper.abstract: We prove that the sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents is entropically continuous for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism, provided the entropy exceeds its second-largest exterior growth rate. We also establish stable strong positive recurrence and show that the topological entropy is continuous, and the number of ergodic measures of maximal entropy is upper semicontinuous. This extends the result of Buzzi, Crovisier, and Sarig to arbitrary dimensions. We give examples in both the measure-theoretic and topological senses, showing that this entropy gap condition is sharp. We also present applications related to the Newhouse phenomenon and standard maps.

analysis.relevance_note: Entropic continuity, topological entropy and maximal-entropy measures are central to the research profile.
analysis.tldr: An entropy gap above the second-largest exterior growth rate gives entropic continuity of positive Lyapunov sums and stability properties in arbitrary dimension.
analysis.problem: Extend entropy-controlled Lyapunov continuity and strong positive recurrence beyond the surface setting.
analysis.main_result: For every \(C^\infty\) diffeomorphism, the sum of positive Lyapunov exponents is entropically continuous provided the entropy exceeds its second-largest exterior growth rate. In the stated gap regime, the authors also establish stable strong positive recurrence, continuity of topological entropy and upper semicontinuity of the number of ergodic measures of maximal entropy, extending the cited Buzzi–Crovisier–Sarig result to arbitrary dimensions. Examples in both measure-theoretic and topological senses show sharpness of the gap condition; applications concern the Newhouse phenomenon and standard maps. The definitions of entropic continuity and the growth rate, precise perturbation setting and proof methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Entropy gaps, Lyapunov exponents, strong positive recurrence and maximal-entropy measures.

paper.title: Independence of Thurston eigenvalues and Lyapunov exponents for quadratic rational maps
paper.abstract: We study post-critically finite quadratic rational maps $f: \mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$ where the two critical points lie in the same cycle. The Thurston eigenvalues of $f$ are those of the derivative of the Thurston pullback map $\sigma_f$ at its fixed point. Addressing questions of Buff--Epstein--Koch, we construct a sequence of real, bitransitive centres in the critical orbit relation curve $C_2$ which degenerates in moduli space, and whose Lyapunov exponents tend to infinity whilst the Thurston eigenvalues satisfy $\frac{1}{10}< |\lambda|<1$. We also show the Thurston eigenvalues across all bitransitive centres in $C_2$ have a spectral gap on compact subsets of the curve.

analysis.relevance_note: Degenerating postcritically finite maps, pullback spectra and Lyapunov exponents give a structural complex-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: A degenerating sequence of real bitransitive quadratic centres has diverging Lyapunov exponents while its Thurston eigenvalues remain bounded away from zero and inside the unit disk.
analysis.problem: Compare Thurston pullback eigenvalues with Lyapunov exponents for quadratic rational maps whose critical points share a cycle.
analysis.main_result: For postcritically finite quadratic rational maps \(f:\mathbb P^1\to\mathbb P^1\) with both critical points in one cycle, Thurston eigenvalues are the eigenvalues of the derivative of the Thurston pullback at its fixed point. A sequence of real bitransitive centres in the critical-orbit relation curve \(C_2\) degenerates in moduli space, with Lyapunov exponents tending to infinity and Thurston eigenvalues satisfying \(1/10<\lvert\lambda\rvert<1\). Across all bitransitive centres in \(C_2\), the Thurston eigenvalues have a spectral gap on compact subsets of the curve. The construction details and quantitative compact-set gap: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Construction of a degenerating sequence of real bitransitive centres
analysis.context: Quadratic rational dynamics, Thurston pullbacks and moduli-space degeneration.

paper.title: Integrable nearest neighbor interaction Hamiltonians and the rigidity of the Toda Lattice
paper.abstract: We consider mechanical Hamiltonian systems, where the potentials describe a nearest-neighbor interaction law. In this setting, a non trivial example of an integrable system is the celebrated Toda lattice. We study deformations of this potential (for three particles), and show that some classes of analytic deformations of the potential break its integrability, without assuming anything about the form of the integrals. This result is reminiscent of local rigidity of ellipses in billiards. The proof relies on the fact that high energy orbits for the Toda lattice approximate billiard orbits in some polytopes.

analysis.relevance_note: Rigidity of integrability and a billiard approximation give a structural smooth-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Certain analytic deformations of the three-particle Toda potential destroy integrability without restrictions on the form of the integrals.
analysis.problem: Study rigidity of integrability for nearest-neighbor interaction Hamiltonians near the three-particle Toda lattice.
analysis.main_result: For mechanical Hamiltonian systems with nearest-neighbor interaction potentials, some classes of analytic deformations of the three-particle Toda potential break integrability, without assumptions on the form of the integrals. The proof uses approximation of billiard orbits in certain polytopes by high-energy Toda orbits. The deformation classes, exact integrability convention and quantitative approximation estimates: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: High-energy Toda-orbit approximation by polytope billiard orbits
analysis.context: Hamiltonian integrability, Toda-lattice rigidity and billiards.

paper.title: Development of a GPU-accelerated numerical simulation model for liver infection in realistic domains
paper.abstract: Viral hepatitis reduces the functionality of the liver and constitutes a major global health concern because it oftentimes evolves to chronic inflammation leading to long term liver damage. Mathematical models on a mesoscopic scale abstract from only partly known cell-scale processes while providing an in-silico tool for understanding tissue-scale development of the disease. In this work, we investigate the interactions between virus and immune cells in a realistic three-dimensional liver geometries by using a reaction-diffusion model that reproduces infection courses with cure and with chronic developments. A GPU-based finite-difference implementation, released as an open-source Python library, achieves speedups greater than x30 for realistic mesh sizes, making three-dimensional simulations on realistic geometries computationally tractable. This provides a basis for future in-silico studies of treatment strategies, such as testing antiviral or immunomodulatory therapies, and for patient-specific simulations based on individual liver geometries, paving the way towards personalized healthcare.

analysis.relevance_note: GPU simulation of reaction-diffusion liver-infection models is computational biological modeling without a central profile connection.

paper.title: Propagation failure for bistable differential equations on periodic trees
paper.abstract: We study traveling fronts for bistable reaction-diffusion equations on periodic heterogeneous trees. We use comparison principles to estimate the pinning and propagation regions for both cubic and general bistabilities. Our analytical results and numerical simulations show that the interesting propagation reversal effects found in homogeneous trees become more pronounced in the heterogeneous setting, paving the way towards understanding more general graphs. As the diffusion strength increases, the waves end up moving in the same direction irrespective of the bistability. This direction is determined solely by the underlying structure of the heterogeneous tree. Our techniques also lead to sharper results for the homogeneous setting.

analysis.relevance_note: Traveling-front pinning and reversal on heterogeneous trees are reaction-diffusion questions without a central entropy, symbolic or dimension component here.

paper.title: Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
paper.abstract: We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincar\'e maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections. For center manifolds, it simultaneously determines the nonlinear reduced dynamics, providing a low-dimensional representation from which nearby invariant objects can be lifted to the original phase space. For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, we derive an equivalent real formulation based on Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations. This allows real-valued jet transport while retaining the advantages of complex spectral coordinates in the cohomological solver. The implementation also incorporates inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling, and a posteriori validation tests. Numerical experiments with a quasi-periodically forced pendulum, an oscillating solar sail in the Earth-Moon system, and a simplified solar system model illustrate the construction and its computational properties. In the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation reduces computation time by approximately a factor of 2.2 compared with the complex implementation.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant manifolds attached to quasiperiodic tori and reduced center dynamics provide a smooth-dynamics connection despite the computational emphasis.
analysis.tldr: A Fourier–Taylor graph method computes local manifolds of known reducible quasiperiodic tori, including center reduced dynamics and a real formulation for complex Floquet pairs.
analysis.problem: Compute invariant manifolds over selected spectral subspaces of reducible quasiperiodic tori in discrete systems.
analysis.main_result: Assuming the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, coefficients of a manifold graph over a selected spectral subspace are computed recursively using jet transport and torus cohomological equations. Stable, unstable and center selections are accommodated; for center manifolds, nonlinear reduced dynamics are determined simultaneously so nearby invariant objects can be lifted. For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations give an equivalent real formulation. The implementation includes inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling and a posteriori validation tests. Experiments involve a forced pendulum, Earth–Moon solar sail and simplified solar system; in the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation is approximately 2.2 times faster than the complex implementation. The precise nonresonance and solvability conditions: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Quasiperiodic invariant tori, Floquet reduction and local invariant manifolds.

paper.title: A Finite Automaton Translating Geometric Addresses into Dynamical Itineraries on the Basilica
paper.abstract: Fractals are generally known for their self-similarity and repeating patterns. One way to produce fractals is via the dynamics of functions from the extended complex plane to itself. These fractals are known as Julia sets. In this paper, we explore how methods from symbolic dynamics and computation theory can be used to describe where points on the basilica Julia set might be located depending on their dynamical orbit under the polynomial function $f(z)=z^2-1$.

analysis.relevance_note: Finite automata, symbolic itineraries and Julia-set addresses directly match symbolic coding and fractal dynamics.
analysis.tldr: Symbolic dynamics and computation theory are used to relate orbit itineraries to positions on the basilica Julia set.
analysis.problem: Translate geometric addresses into dynamical itineraries on the basilica.
analysis.main_result: The paper explores how symbolic dynamics and computation theory describe possible locations of points on the basilica Julia set from their orbits under \(f(z)=z^2-1\). The title specifies a finite automaton translating geometric addresses into itineraries. The automaton states, transition rules, exact coding statement and treatment of address ambiguity: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Symbolic coding of the basilica Julia set.

paper.title: Prevalence of the periodicity of maximizing measures
paper.abstract: For a continuous map $T\colon X\rightarrow X$ on a compact metric space $(X,d)$, we say that a function $f\colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ has the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ if its time averages along forward orbits of $T$ are maximized at a periodic orbit. In this article, we establish the Hunt--Ott conjecture (cf.~\cite{HO96a,HO96b}), that is, the property $\mathscr{P}_T$ is prevalent (in the sense of Hunt--Sauer--Yorke) in the space of Lipschitz functions with respect to a standard metric for subshifts of finite type. This result is a strengthening of \cite[Theorem~A]{BZ16} and \cite[Theorem~1.1]{DLZ24}, confirms the prediction mentioned in the ICM proceeding contribution of Bochi (\cite[Section~1]{Boc18}) suggested by experimental evidence.

analysis.relevance_note: Maximizing measures and prevalence for Lipschitz functions on shifts of finite type directly concern symbolic ergodic optimization.
analysis.tldr: For shifts of finite type with a standard metric, functions whose forward time averages are maximized at a periodic orbit form a prevalent set in the Lipschitz space.
analysis.problem: Establish prevalence of periodic maximization in symbolic dynamics.
analysis.main_result: For a continuous map \(T:X\to X\) of a compact metric space, property \(\mathscr P_T\) means that forward-orbit time averages of a real function are maximized at a periodic orbit. The authors prove that this property is prevalent in the Hunt–Sauer–Yorke sense in the Lipschitz-function space for subshifts of finite type with respect to a standard metric, thereby establishing the stated Hunt–Ott conjecture. The abstract does not assert uniqueness of the maximizing measure. The specific standard metric, prevalence witness and proof techniques: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Ergodic optimization, prevalence and shifts of finite type.

paper.title: Territorial Conflict as a Cellular Automaton: Frozen Domains and Active Fronts in a Risk-Derived Local Rule
paper.abstract: We formulate the attack and fortification rules of the game Risk as a synchronous cellular automaton on a graph, with battles resolved by exact dice odds. We prove, and verify in Lean, that for the default exchange ratio the rule has radius 6, or 5 for deterministic battles with a positive attack threshold, both attained; that its deterministic form is irreversible except at the highest attack thresholds without growth and with fortification absent or inactive; that without troop growth it freezes in finite time; and that the dynamics near an interface is locally determined. The coupling of the ownership field to a troop field separates frozen domains from active fronts: with a positive attack threshold, saturated domains cannot be conquered, while interfaces with heterogeneous troops keep fighting. In 14252 runs, with attractors classified operationally in Wolfram's scheme, raising the attack threshold takes the system from dominance by one faction to a frozen fragmented partition. The share of the largest faction drops between the same two threshold values at every size up to L=128, in a step about 0.5 wide under a continuous threshold (L=64-96), whereas the probability of complete consolidation is a size-dependent crossover governed by saturated minority domains. Long-period attractors combine spatially fixed local oscillators; apparent class-IV gliders are artefacts of index-ordered tie-breaking. Straight fronts stayed within two cells of their initial position for up to 500,000 steps, over which they are one-dimensional automata with non-recurrent, incompressible dynamics and positive Lyapunov speeds, constant for L>=48. Compared with mean-field and random-regular-graph controls, the lattice lengthens conflicts about twentyfold and clusters conquest: a cell next to a fresh conquest is about five times as likely as average to be conquered next, against 1.1-1.5 in the controls.

analysis.relevance_note: Rigorous radius, irreversibility and freezing statements concern the structural dynamics of a cellular automaton; simulation claims remain distinct from theorems.
analysis.tldr: A Risk-derived graph cellular automaton has proved locality and freezing properties, while simulations explore domains, fronts and operational attractor classes.
analysis.problem: Describe structural and observed dynamics of coupled ownership and troop fields under local attack and fortification rules.
analysis.main_result: The synchronous graph rule uses exact dice odds. For the default exchange ratio its radius is six, or five for deterministic battles with a positive attack threshold, with both attained; these statements are proved and verified in Lean. The deterministic form is irreversible except at the stated highest-threshold, no-growth cases with fortification absent or inactive. Without troop growth it freezes in finite time, and interface dynamics are locally determined. With a positive attack threshold, saturated domains cannot be conquered, whereas heterogeneous troop interfaces continue fighting. In 14,252 runs, operational Wolfram classes shift from faction dominance to frozen fragmentation as the threshold rises; long-period attractors combine fixed local oscillators, and apparent class-IV gliders arise from index-ordered tie-breaking. Straight fronts remain within two cells for up to 500,000 steps; non-recurrence, incompressibility and positive Lyapunov speeds describe these tested fronts, not an independently stated infinite-time theorem. The exact update formula, threshold exceptions and statistical uncertainty: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Cellular-automaton locality, irreversibility, frozen domains and interface dynamics.

paper.title: Syringe reuse in HCV transmission among people who inject drugs: behavioral thresholds and optimal control
paper.abstract: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) transmission among people who inject drugs (PWID) is driven largely by syringe sharing and reuse, yet existing models rarely treat reuse as a behavior that individuals adopt and abandon. In this work, we develop and analyze a four-compartment epidemic model that explicitly incorporates syringe reuse as a distinct behavioral process, introducing a high-risk susceptible subgroup that acquires infection through both direct contact and syringe-mediated transmission. We establish the well-posedness and biological feasibility of the model, derive the basic reproduction number, and analyze the existence and stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria along with closed-form behavioral threshold conditions for syringe-reuse adoption and cessation. Global sensitivity and scenario analyses reveal that while transmission and recovery parameters dominate epidemic potential, behavioral parameters governing the adoption and cessation of syringe reuse play a crucial role in disease persistence and control thresholds. The model's projected infection dynamics are broadly consistent with observed U.S. HCV incidence trends. We further formulate an optimal control problem targeting reuse initiation and cessation, and show through cost-effectiveness analysis that combined behavioral interventions outperform single-component strategies in reducing both infection and high-risk behavior. These results indicate that behavioral prevention aimed at syringe reuse is a necessary component of sustained HCV control among PWID.

analysis.relevance_note: Syringe-reuse epidemic thresholds and optimal behavioral control are applied population modeling without a central strongest-interest theme.

paper.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
paper.abstract: We prove Mosher's Transverse Finiteness Conjecture, posed in 1996. This states that every taut, finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows, up to orbit equivalence. Our strategy is to organize the flows that are almost transverse to $\mathcal F$ using their associated universal circles. This technique also establishes the following rigidity result: if a finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ is almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow $\varphi$ without perfect fits, then $\varphi$ is the unique pseudo-Anosov flow that is almost transverse to $\mathcal F$, up to orbit equivalence. In fact, in this setting, $\mathcal F$ has only one minimal universal circle.

analysis.relevance_note: Finiteness and rigidity up to orbit equivalence make topological flow classification central.
analysis.tldr: A taut finite-depth foliation of an atoroidal three-manifold is almost transverse to only finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows up to orbit equivalence.
analysis.problem: Prove transverse finiteness and a uniqueness result for pseudo-Anosov flows using universal circles.
analysis.main_result: The authors prove Mosher’s Transverse Finiteness Conjecture: every taut finite-depth foliation \(\mathcal F\) of an atoroidal three-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows up to orbit equivalence. The flows are organized by their associated universal circles. If a finite-depth foliation \(\mathcal F\) is almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow \(\varphi\) without perfect fits, then \(\varphi\) is the unique such flow up to orbit equivalence; in this setting \(\mathcal F\) has only one minimal universal circle. The numerical finiteness bound and detailed universal-circle construction: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Organization of almost-transverse flows by associated universal circles
analysis.context: Pseudo-Anosov flows, finite-depth foliations, orbit equivalence and universal circles.

paper.title: Global dynamics of impulsive reaction-diffusion systems with asymptotically unbounded domain
paper.abstract: This paper is devoted to the study of the global dynamics of continuous-discrete hybrid population models with an asymptotically unbounded domain. We first prove a global attractivity result for a class of impulsive reaction-diffusion equations whose diffusion coefficients vanish asymptotically. A cut-off function is combined with an auxiliary impulsive kinetic system to construct a subsolution that is compatible with the birth update at every cycle. We then use comparison arguments to establish threshold-type dynamics for the original model when the birth function is either monotone or nonmonotone. It turns out that the threshold value for extinction and persistence is explicitly determined by the birth pulse, the within-cycle growth, and the asymptotic expansion rate of the habitat.

analysis.relevance_note: Extinction and persistence thresholds for impulsive population reaction-diffusion models are PDE-centered applied dynamics without a central profile theme.

paper.title: Controlability of the 1D wave equation by point sources: outgoing states, circle rotations and small divisors
paper.abstract: We characterise the states reachable from rest for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line driven by finitely many fixed point sources. The characterisation reduces the control problem to a cohomological equation on a circle whose length is twice the distance between the outermost sources, with support constraints determined by the control time. For two sources, the reachable set is closed and the controls are unique at every finite time. For three sources, we give a complete classification in terms of the control time and the ratio of the two relevant travel times. Below the time needed to traverse the outer interval twice, reachability is described by finite orbit sums. At and above this threshold, an irrational ratio produces a dense, non-closed reachable set in the compatible outgoing-state space, and exact reachability is determined by a small-divisor condition. We also quantify the cost of control. The minimum control norm is equivalent to the energy norm of the target plus a weighted Fourier norm of its periodised defect. For a badly approximable irrational ratio, the worst cost for defects of Fourier degree at most $N$ grows linearly in $N$, i.e. Liouville ratios produce superpolynomial growth along subsequences. We derive constructive approximation estimates and sharp worst-case cost--accuracy rates on Sobolev classes of defects. For an arbitrary number of sources, the long-time classification and the quantitative estimates are governed by simultaneous Diophantine approximation of the source positions.

analysis.relevance_note: Circle rotations, cohomological equations and Diophantine small divisors provide a substantial connection despite the wave-control application.
analysis.tldr: Reachability for point-driven wave equations reduces to circle cohomology, with rationality and small divisors controlling closure and control cost.
analysis.problem: Characterize outgoing states reachable from rest by finitely many fixed point sources for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line.
analysis.main_result: The control problem reduces to a cohomological equation on a circle of length twice the outermost-source distance, with support constraints set by control time. With two sources, the reachable set is closed and controls are unique at every finite time. With three sources, finite orbit sums describe reachability below the time to traverse the outer interval twice. At and above that threshold, an irrational travel-time ratio gives a dense nonclosed reachable set in the compatible outgoing-state space, and exact reachability requires a small-divisor condition. The minimum control norm is equivalent to target energy plus a weighted Fourier norm of the periodized defect. For badly approximable irrational ratios the worst cost for Fourier degree at most \(N\) grows linearly in \(N\); Liouville ratios give superpolynomial growth along subsequences. Constructive approximation and sharp worst-case Sobolev cost–accuracy rates are derived. For arbitrarily many sources, simultaneous Diophantine approximation governs long-time classification and estimates. The exact small-divisor weights and rate formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Circle rotations, Diophantine approximation and wave-equation reachability.

paper.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
paper.abstract: Every finite population is eventually driven to extinction by demographic noise, even when the deterministic dynamics have a stable coexistence state. We develop a large-deviation theory of this process for hierarchical food webs of arbitrary size. In a community of $N$ species, the basal species $X_1$ reproduces intrinsically and every consumer may prey on all species below it, so that omnivory is built into the interaction graph. For unit conversion efficiency and self-limitation confined to the basal species, the mean-field dynamics have at most $2^{N-1}+1$ feasible fixed points. We prove that the sign of each passive eigenvalue equals the sign of the extinct species' density in the enlarged community, that every partial community containing $X_1$ is a saddle with one unstable direction for each extinct consumer, and that the coexistence state is the only stable fixed point. A WKB treatment of the master equation gives a $2N$-dimensional Hamiltonian whose fluctuational fixed points are obtained in closed form. The resulting extinction network has $3^{N-1}$ fluctuation-driven transitions, and its coarse-grained dynamics yield an exact recursion for every mean extinction time. We analyse the three-species omnivory module in full, including a minimal set of existence conditions, global stability of coexistence, numerical instanton actions for all nine transitions and the most probable extinction route, which we confirm with stochastic simulations. Finally, we show how deleting a single trophic link reshapes the extinction network.

analysis.relevance_note: Large-deviation extinction networks in hierarchical food webs are ecological stochastic modeling without a central entropy or symbolic-dynamics theme.

paper.title: On Grokking and the Dynamics of Generalization
paper.abstract: We extend the signal-channel theory of grokking introduced by Litman and Guo by relating training dissipation and evaluation transfer to population risk. For preconditioned gradient flows with time-dependent kernels, we distinguish two sources of limited evaluation visibility, namely small cumulative dissipation and weak transfer. We obtain quantitative bounds for task visibility and establish their stability under signal filtering and changes of evaluation distribution. We describe how task directions enter the effective signal channel through spectral activation or transport. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the transferred signal to decrease squared population risk and derive classification error bounds under margin assumptions. These results yield sufficient conditions for the same training trajectory to generalize under one evaluation distribution while failing under another. We show that differences in spectral learning rates can produce arbitrarily long delays between low training loss and low population risk. By relating classification accuracy to the distribution of margin crossing times, we construct a family of gradient flows in which the generalization delay tends to infinity, while both the duration of the transition from zero to full accuracy and the corresponding variation of population risk tend to zero. These phenomena occur without feature evolution during training. Finally, we prove that the occurrence and timing of generalization cannot generally be inferred from training dynamics alone, but depend on the geometry of evaluation transfer and its relation to the target.

analysis.relevance_note: Gradient-flow generalization and evaluation-transfer bounds concern machine learning rather than the strongest dynamical research interests.

paper.title: Structure Preserving Iterative Solution of Linear Systems Arising in Gauss Collocation for port-Hamiltonian DAEs
paper.abstract: This work presents structure-preserving computational techniques for the pencil Pad\'e approximation arising in the numerical integration of port-Hamiltonian differential-algebraic equations (pH-DAEs) via the Gauss-Legendre schemes. We first extend the concept of the diagonal Pad\'e approximation and introduce a generalized framework characterizing the $s$-stage Gauss method. We further examine its structural properties and the role of the full orthogonalization method (FOM) in approximating the discrete solution. Building on this, we analyze the iterative approximation of the pencil Pade approximation and establish conditions on the search space in Petrov-Galerkin-type approximations which guarantee that structure-induced properties, such as dissipativity or energy preservation, are inherited by the Petrov-Galerkin approximations. In particular, we show that FOM-based Krylov subspace methods preserve these properties iterate-wise. The presented results provide a new insight into the interplay between Krylov subspace methods and energy preservation in the numerical integration of pH-DAEs. Finally, we conclude with numerical examples illustrating the convergence and the conservation of the physical properties.

analysis.relevance_note: Krylov methods preserving energy and dissipativity in numerical differential-algebraic integration are computational analysis without a central profile connection.

paper.title: Milk-removal feedback shapes lactation sustainability and daily output in a model of human lactation
paper.abstract: Milk production during lactation is dynamically regulated by milk removal, yet quantitative models linking feeding or pumping schedules to subsequent production remain scarce. We develop a minimal model describing milk accumulation and production between removal sessions, and the stimulation of subsequent production through milk removal. We compare different assumptions about how stimulation depends on the amount of milk removed or the duration of removal, and consider two removal protocols: prescribing either the removed amount or the removal duration. When stimulation depends on the removed amount, declining production can reduce subsequent stimulation and reinforce the decline. This leads to a critical wait interval beyond which no repeated constant schedule can sustain lactation. If stimulation is inefficient for small removal amounts but more efficient at intermediate amounts, the model can exhibit bistability: depending on the initial conditions, milk production either persists or ceases. In contrast, duration-dependent stimulation does not permit a zero-production state under continued removal, but can generate non-constant long-term dynamics under certain conditions. We further show that maximizing milk removal per session need not maximize daily output, because increased removal competes with session frequency. The framework provides a basis for testing alternative feedback hypotheses against longitudinal data and for optimizing feeding and pumping schedules.

analysis.relevance_note: Feedback and removal schedules in a lactation model are biological applied dynamics without a central symbolic, entropy or geometric-dimension component.

paper.title: Stochastic extinction: convergence in distribution
paper.abstract: We develop a general framework to show the convergence in distribution of non-irreducible Markov processes to invariant distributions supported on lower-dimensional subsets of the state space. In applications, these singular supports signal the emergence of distinctive long-time behaviours, such as the extinction of species in ecology and the concentration on laminar states in fluid dynamics. The proposed approach is made widely applicable by tailoring its assumptions so that they can be verified using the theory of stochastic persistence/extinction. We illustrate the framework by applying it to stochastic perturbations of the Lorenz and Rosenzweig-MacArthur models and to a general two-dimensional Kolmogorov system.

analysis.relevance_note: Convergence to invariant distributions with singular supports gives a direct invariant-measure connection across stochastic dynamical models.
analysis.tldr: A general framework proves distributional convergence of nonirreducible Markov processes to invariant laws supported on lower-dimensional subsets.
analysis.problem: Establish convergence to singular invariant distributions in stochastic extinction regimes.
analysis.main_result: The framework treats nonirreducible Markov processes converging in distribution to invariant laws supported on lower-dimensional state-space subsets. Its assumptions are tailored for verification by stochastic persistence/extinction theory. Applications include stochastic perturbations of the Lorenz and Rosenzweig–MacArthur models and a general two-dimensional Kolmogorov system; singular supports describe species extinction or concentration on laminar states in the motivating settings. The explicit assumptions, limiting laws and convergence rates: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Singular invariant distributions, nonirreducible Markov dynamics and extinction.

paper.title: A Short Proof of the Goldman--Parker Conjecture
paper.abstract: Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres. We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction. For parameters just below the critical value, we use the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple product of the reflections. This wall and one of its cusp translates bound a strip from which we construct a trapping region. At the critical value $\tan^2 A=125/3$, the two fixed points merge, and the same construction applies to the limiting wall.

analysis.relevance_note: Discreteness and faithfulness of complex-hyperbolic reflection-group representations directly concern geometric group actions.
analysis.tldr: A geometric trapping-region construction gives a short proof of the Goldman–Parker discreteness-and-faithfulness criterion, including its critical endpoint.
analysis.problem: Prove discreteness and faithfulness for ideal-triangle reflection representations in complex hyperbolic geometry.
analysis.main_result: Three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant \(A\) define a discrete faithful representation of \(\mathbb Z/2\ast\mathbb Z/2\ast\mathbb Z/2\) in \(PU(2,1)\) whenever \(\tan^2 A\leq125/3\). The authors give a shorter geometric proof of this previously proved Goldman–Parker conjecture. For parameters just below the critical value, the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple reflection product and one cusp translate bound a strip used to build a trapping region. At \(\tan^2 A=125/3\), the fixed points merge and the construction uses the limiting wall. The complete wall equations and trapping estimates: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Complex-hyperbolic reflection-group actions and discrete faithful representations.

paper.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
paper.abstract: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $\Gamma$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $\Gamma$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.

analysis.relevance_note: Expanding group actions, spectral-gap connections and invariant-measure uniqueness directly match group-action interests.
analysis.tldr: Expanding isometry-group actions yield measurable equidecompositions and uniqueness of finitely additive invariant measure in non-Archimedean settings.
analysis.problem: Establish measurable equidecomposability and a Banach–Ruziewicz theorem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields.
analysis.main_result: Let \(\mathbb K\) be a number-field completion at a non-Archimedean place and \(n\geq2\). Any two bounded Haar-measurable subsets of \(\mathbb K^n\) with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure are equidecomposable into finitely many Haar-measurable pieces by a certain countable group \(\Gamma\) of affine isometries. Up to a constant factor, Haar measure is the unique nonzero finitely additive \(\Gamma\)-invariant measure on bounded Haar-measurable subsets. Both results follow from expansion of the \(\Gamma\) action, closely related to spectral gap. For \(n=1\) in arbitrary characteristic, analogous results hold when the residue field is not prime, using countable isometry groups that need not be affine. The group construction and quantitative expansion constants: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Measurable equidecompositions, non-Archimedean group actions and invariant measures.

paper.title: Generic bi-stochastic semigroups are flows
paper.abstract: We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, \mu)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, \mu)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, \mu)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces. This enables the construction of stochastic processes, via which dilations and thereby $\mathrm{PW}$-approximations may be obtained. In a similar fashion, we demonstrate the weak-genericity of weakly-continuous measure-preserving flows on $(X, \mu)$ within the space of $\mathcal{C}_{0}$-semigroups of bi-stochastic operators on $L^{2}(X, \mu)$. To achieve this, we make use of random measures (viz. Poisson point processes) and build on our discrete-time result. This complements recent advances in ergodic theory due to Furlong on the genericity of measure-preserving flows in the space of measure-preserving semi-flows.

analysis.relevance_note: Genericity of measure-preserving transformations and flows directly concerns structural ergodic dynamics and actions.
analysis.tldr: Invertible measure-preserving transformations are generic among bistochastic operators in the weak polynomial topology, with an analogous weak-genericity theorem for flows.
analysis.problem: Relate generic bistochastic operators and semigroups to invertible measure-preserving dynamics.
analysis.main_result: For a standard probability space \((X,\mu)\), the space \(\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)\) is generic within bistochastic operators on \(L^2(X,\mu)\) for the weak polynomial topology. A reformulation of the Birkhoff–von Neumann theorem for infinite-dimensional bistochastic operators enables stochastic-process constructions, dilations and the stated polynomial-weak approximations. Weakly continuous measure-preserving flows are also weak-generic among \(\mathcal C_0\)-semigroups of bistochastic operators, using Poisson point processes and the discrete-time result. The precise topology definitions, approximation estimates and additional probability-space qualifications: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Generic measure-preserving transformations, flows and bistochastic semigroups.

paper.title: Critical exponents and near-critical limits for random matrix products
paper.abstract: We study the approach to the zero-Lyapunov-exponent transition for products of independent, identically distributed invertible matrices. The matrix laws are supported in a common compact subset of $GL(d,\mathbb{R})$ and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible and proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. We establish a near-critical renewal theorem for the occupation measure and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle as well as exact asymptotics and scaling limits for three observables describing the transient dynamics. The expected number of escapes from the unit ball and the expected number of visits to a fixed annulus diverge as the inverse absolute Lyapunov exponent, and both counts have exponential limits after normalization. The time spent on the side opposite to the asymptotic drift has critical exponent two and converges, after rescaling, to the positive occupation time of Brownian motion with negative drift.

analysis.relevance_note: Lyapunov exponents, logarithmic cocycles and occupation statistics give a substantial random-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Near a zero top-Lyapunov exponent, renewal and diffusion limits determine critical scaling for escape, annulus visits and opposite-drift occupation.
analysis.problem: Determine transient observables near the zero-Lyapunov transition for independent identically distributed matrix products.
analysis.main_result: The invertible matrix laws share a common compact support in \(GL(d,\mathbb R)\) and converge in total variation to a strongly irreducible proximal law with zero top Lyapunov exponent. The authors prove a near-critical occupation-measure renewal theorem and a functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle. Expected escape counts from the unit ball and visit counts to a fixed annulus diverge inversely with the absolute Lyapunov exponent; normalized counts have exponential limits. Opposite-drift occupation time has critical exponent two and, after rescaling, converges to positive occupation time of Brownian motion with negative drift. The normalization constants and precise renewal hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Functional diffusion limit for the logarithmic cocycle
analysis.context: Random matrix products, Lyapunov transitions and occupation measures.

paper.title: Limit laws for Siegel theta sums
paper.abstract: Siegel theta sums are exponential sums over the integer lattice whose phases are determined by a quadratic form. For a random choice of quadratic form, we prove a limit law for the modulus of the normalised sum as the summation range tends to infinity. The limiting distribution depends on the space from which the quadratic form is sampled. We prove precise heavy-tail asymptotics for random sampling from (a) the full space of quadratic forms and (b) the space of diagonal forms. This study extends classic results by Jurkat and Van Horne for one-variable theta sums and by G\"otze and Gordin for theta series on Siegel half-spaces. Our approach uses the Shale--Weil representation of the metaplectic group and the ergodic theory of unipotent flows.

analysis.relevance_note: Unipotent-flow ergodic theory and a metaplectic-group representation supply a homogeneous-dynamics connection to theta-sum statistics.
analysis.tldr: Random quadratic forms yield limiting laws for normalized Siegel theta-sum moduli, with precise heavy tails depending on the sampling space.
analysis.problem: Determine limit distributions and heavy tails of Siegel theta sums for random quadratic forms.
analysis.main_result: As the summation range grows, the modulus of the normalized lattice exponential sum has a limiting law for a random quadratic form. The law depends on the sampling space, and precise heavy-tail asymptotics are proved for the full space of quadratic forms and for diagonal forms. The approach uses the Shale–Weil representation of the metaplectic group and ergodic theory of unipotent flows. The normalization, sampling measures, limiting distributions and heavy-tail exponents: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Shale–Weil representation of the metaplectic group
analysis.context: Siegel theta sums, homogeneous dynamics and heavy-tailed limit laws.

paper.title: The Brownian L\'evy transformation is exact
paper.abstract: We prove that the L\'evy transformation of Brownian motion is exact. This settles the long-standing question of whether the transformation is ergodic. The proof combines an interval cutting argument with an estimate for the first entrance of the iterated paths into a small neighborhood of zero at an independent exponential time.

analysis.relevance_note: Exactness and ergodicity are structural invariant-measure properties, giving a clear ergodic-theory connection.
analysis.tldr: The author proves exactness of the Brownian Lévy transformation, thereby settling its ergodicity question.
analysis.problem: Establish exactness of the Lévy transformation of Brownian motion.
analysis.main_result: The Brownian Lévy transformation is proved exact. The abstract identifies this as settling the long-standing ergodicity question. The proof combines an interval-cutting argument with a first-entrance estimate for iterated paths into a small neighborhood of zero at an independent exponential time. The entrance bound and precise exactness criterion: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: First-entrance estimate at an independent exponential time
analysis.context: Brownian transformations, exactness and ergodicity.

paper.title: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
paper.abstract: We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts. Second, approximate the full evolution operator using a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki (LTS) decomposition of the desired approximation order in time step. The I-LTS construction ensures that the full evolution operator can be represented as a product of terms that each have an efficient explicit tensor product factorization that can be handled efficiently with tensor network and/or quantum block-encoding methods. Next, we apply this method to an important non-integrable point example of a dynamical system: the Stepanoff flow on the torus. First, we derive an efficient unitary quantum algorithm for simulating the Stepanoff flow that can be thought of as a unitary classical version of a quantum map. Then, we provide a detailed description of the encoding of the two-dimensional system into an efficient quantum circuit, including an efficient block-encoding for all required operators. An efficient Hamiltonian simulation algorithm is constructed using a sequence of alternating quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) and Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) circuits. Finally, the circuit is simulated using a numerical emulator of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and the results are found to be consistent with several alternative classical computational methods. While efficient, the need for Trotterization introduces fundamental complexity in requiring small enough time step for an accurate approximation and solving for the transfer operator requires one to confront the linear scaling of the advection operator with grid size.

analysis.relevance_note: Transfer-operator simulation for a torus flow gives an indirect dynamical-systems connection, although the contribution is primarily computational.
analysis.tldr: An integrable Lie–Trotter–Suzuki splitting produces unitary simulation circuits for the Stepanoff flow, with numerical agreement and explicit complexity limitations.
analysis.problem: Construct efficient unitary time integration by splitting nonlinear generators into integrable parts.
analysis.main_result: The generator is expressed as a sum of integrable parts and its evolution approximated by a Lie–Trotter–Suzuki decomposition of the desired time-step order. Each factor admits an efficient explicit tensor-product factorization for tensor-network or quantum block-encoding methods. For the Stepanoff flow on the torus, the authors construct a quantum circuit with required block encodings, alternating quantum Fourier transforms and quantum signal-processing circuits. A fault-tolerant quantum-computer emulator agrees with alternative classical computations. Trotterization still requires sufficiently small steps, and the advection operator scales linearly with grid size in the transfer-operator problem. The detailed error bounds and resource estimates: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Unitary simulation of the Stepanoff torus flow and transfer operators.

paper.title: Variational approach to droplet motion on uneven solid surfaces, including contact line dynamics and evaporation
paper.abstract: We show how dynamical equations for liquid films and drops on uneven surfaces, including contact line dynamics and evaporation/condensation effects, may be formulated as a variational dynamics, generated via Onsager's variational principle. The theory applies in the isothermal overdamped-dynamics limit. We apply this general approach to obtain several well-known results on contact line dynamics and to study drops pinning and sliding on inclined corrugated surfaces. This approach constructs the dynamical equations starting from the free energy of the system and therefore has the advantage that it naturally incorporates the correct equilibrium properties.

analysis.relevance_note: Onsager variational modeling of liquid films and droplet motion is physical PDE dynamics rather than thermodynamic formalism in the research-profile sense.

paper.title: A zero-one law for one-shot system identification
paper.abstract: Can a model be identified from one experiment? We study analytic systems that are linearly parameterized by a combination of prescribed dictionary terms, such as partial differential operators and dynamical systems. For a single input-response pair, recovery is possible exactly when the evaluated dictionary terms are linearly independent. We prove a sharp zero-one law: either no input uniquely determines the coefficients, or almost every random input sampled from a nondegenerate Gaussian measure does. This dichotomy reduces one-shot system identification to a question about degenerate inputs and provides an a posteriori certificate in the noiseless setting. Numerical examples recover dynamical systems, nonlinear partial differential equations, and structured matrix families from single trajectory data, while also detecting when an extra probe is necessary.

analysis.relevance_note: One-experiment analytic-system identification and Gaussian-input recovery certificates are mainly model-identification questions without a central profile theme.
